3:_: From plaster. Baer Heitev. And see in responsum of Noda BiYehudah Mahadura Tinyana siman 13 regarding tzurat hapetach that the korah above is placed on one side on the asherah — we have no concern with it, but it should not rest on the thickness of the wall itself, for on any wall it does not help that it rise in place of the reed of tzurat hapetach unless there is something protruding from the wall as Magen Avraham wrote in s.k. 28 — see there:
4:_: (In Shulchan Aruch seif 15) And it is required that he place it on the walls of the mavo — and he wrote in responsum of Noda BiYehudah Mahadura Tinyana siman 41: in a breach more than ten [amot] they made upright reeds one opposite the other and on one reed a large korah like a door on its hinge; but most of the time the rotation of the korah is toward the outside and the breach remains open — there is no reliance on the korah at all as amaltara, and because of the reed that is lechi it does not help for width of ten; especially if the reed is distant nine [tefachim] from the beginning of the breach it does not help as lechi and there is no permission — see there:
5:_: (In Shulchan Aruch seif 26) The common practice etc. — and see in Bekhor Shor daf 113 that those reeds of tzurat hapetach must not be distant from the wall three [tefachim]. And also one should not raise the reeds from the ground three [tefachim]; and likewise one may permit not to place the reeds behind the wall when the reeds are not visible from inside within the mavo or opposite the airspace of the mavo as Shulchan Aruch wrote regarding lechi in seif 9 — see there; and see in responsum of Beit Efraim siman 28 explained at length that the words of Eshel Avraham on this are clarified like a new garment — see there in the name of Sefer Mekor Chayim that specifically when the two reeds are distant; but when one side is adjacent to the house it is valid — and there I wrote that tzurat hapetach from a reed protruding from the projection of the wall like lechi — Tosafos Shabbos wrote to prove that it must be a width of a tefach like for lechi, and it is not required — see there; and also in seif 26 everything is explained well — and see what Peri Megadim Orach Chayim part 1 siman 28 wrote there:
7:_: Under. See in responsum of Beit Efraim, and see at the end of Sefer Mekor Chayim on the laws of Pesach regarding correction of eruv that if one places the reeds inside the house until one amah within the fence enclosed on four sides it is nothing — see there; and it appears from his words that even if one reed is outside it does not help:
9:_: The sea. Baer Heitev. And see in Chacham Tzvi siman 37 that wrote that England and Scotland and the like whose sea is their wall surrounding them and they are high from the ground of the sea much — they are liable for reshut ha-rabbim and bridges and planks in them require correction like other cities that are not enclosed, because the public comes and nullifies the partition since they are not made by human hands — see there; and see in responsum of Beit Efraim on this matter and in the words of Chacham Tzvi on this everything is explained well; and see in responsum of Ohel Yaakov siman 47 who also wrote regarding correcting a city for vows that there is empty space from the enclosure until the wall more than ten amot — opposite it there are stakes driven in the ground with three [tefachim] between one and its fellow, and on the heads of the stakes a korah or korot fixed on every side; and he wrote that since there is three [tefachim] space it does not help, and also this is not tzurat hapetach since they rely mainly on proof that it was not made for tzurat hapetach but for partition, and a partition with three [tefachim] space does not help — see there he wrote that even if one makes tzurat hapetach there is no way to make tzurat hapetach adjacent to each other, and specifically in a breach of less than thirty amot one places tzurat hapetach between them and a side of breach less than ten remains — it is nothing; and if the breach was more than thirty tzurat hapetach within ten does not help since on every side there remains measure of breach and a way to make many openings we say, but a way to make all openings or adjacent to each other we do not say — see there:
12:_: And with this. Baer Heitev. And see in Emunat Shmuel siman 40 when the ditch was closed by earth and stones — if the closing does not rise more than ten amot behold it is like an opening and does not forbid; but if it is more than ten amot behold it is like a breach; and see in responsum of Chacham Tzvi siman 5 that the law of a city surrounded by a ditch ten deep and four wide is like a city enclosed by a wall high with doors and bar, and therefore he permitted carrying in the city of Aachen — see there; and so he also wrote in responsum of Ohel Yaakov siman 73 regarding permission to carry in the city of Aachen; but he wrote there are bridges over which one passes from this side to the other side of the karmelit, and he permitted regarding that the bridges should not be fixed with nails or building but movable and taken at any time they need to raise them with chains and they are like fit to be taken — through raising them the city would be locked and enclosed; and even if they were fixed nevertheless there is tzurat hapetach in the middle of the bridges, and since its open head is to the karmelit tzurat hapetach suffices; and therefore through acquiring permission in eruv and leaving there a remainder without eruv for recognition it is permitted to carry — see there that even if the bridges that are not fixed are closed with a key nevertheless they are fit to be taken — through raising the bridges and closing the key it is not fixed but temporary and is not comparable to sunk in earth that lacks action — see there; and see Noda BiYehudah Mahadura Tinyana siman 42 who also wrote regarding a city whose breach is entirely on the fourth side only that the river goes alongside the city and the ground of the city is ten tefachim higher from the water — only that there is a bridge wider than ten — one must make tzurat hapetach on the bridge — see there; and see in Knesset Yehzekiel 62:3–4 and in Shevut Yaakov siman 17 and in Shevut Yaakov part 3 siman 28. He wrote in Be'er HaGolah: or in Rotterdam that the water is their wall — one should permit; and see in Even HaEzer and in Mor UKtziah what they wrote regarding rivers whose way is to freeze on the words of Taz on this; and see in Eshel Avraham what he wrote in the name of Knesset HaGedolah — see there that if there is a height of ten from the frozen water one should permit in simplicity — see there:
